sentences.text: B. Narender Goud, vs The State Of Telangana on 7 April, 2025

Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Honourable Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.10425 Of 2025
Order:

(ORAL) Heard Mr. M. Sreekanth, learned counsel for the petitioner, and Mr. Putta Krishna Reddy,
Standing Counsel for Municipalities, for respondent No.3.
2.

It appears, in the year 1981, under the Central Government Sponsored Scheme namely Integrated Development of Small & Medium Town (IDSMT) Scheme, respondent No.3 acquired the land to an extent of Acs.07-82 cents in Survey No.773, Acs.07-62 cents in Survey No.774 and Acs.03-41 cents in Survey No.775 situated at Gadwal Mandal and Town by paying compensation to the original owners and pattadars as per the Award under the provisions of Land Acquisition Act.

entities.text: Integrated Development of Small & Medium Town (IDSMT) Scheme
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Subsequently,
respondent No.3 has made the layout into 485 residential plots dividing it into four categories i.e.,
HIG (28 plots), MIG (115 plots), LIG (185 plots) and EWS (157 plots).
The plots have been allotted to the prospective successful winners in the drawal of lots by respondent No.3 as per the rates fixed by the Government under IDSMT Scheme.
3. In the drawal of lots, the petitioner was allotted Plot No.91 in MIG category of size 45 x 60 feet (300 sq. yards).
Similarly, other persons were also allotted plots in drawal of lots.
The petitioner was directed to pay a sum of Rs.78,000/- towards purchase of Plot No.91 in MIG category and the entire amount was paid by the petitioner.
4. According to the petitioner, 185 LIG plots were advertised for sale by drawal of lots, however there was no demand.
60 LIG plots remained unsold.

Thereafter, employees of respondent No.3 Municipality made a request for allotment of such unsold 60 LIG plots exclusively to them and the Government accorded permission to respondent No.3 Municipality for allotment of 51 LIG plots to its employees vide G.O.Rt.No.1680, MA, dated 22.12.1993.
5.
It is submitted that out of total 485 plots, 407 plots were registered in favour of the beneficiaries/allottees and they have constructed houses.
78 plots were left over pending registration.
Registration could not be done due to disputes between respondent No.3 and the Wakf Board.

Contending that they have paid total cost of the plots under IDSMT Scheme, about 78 plots owners have approached this Court by filing W.P.No.33172 of 2011 seeking for a direction to respondent No.3 to execute the sale deeds in their favour.

That writ petition was disposed of vide order dated 06.03.2012 directing respondent Nos.2 to 4 to finalize the issue of registration of house sites stated to have been allotted to the petitioners therein provided the entire cost of the plots is paid.

Thereafter, alleging non- compliance of the order dated 06.03.2012, C.C,No.2124 of 2012 was B. Narender Goud, vs The State Of Telangana on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12680300/

sentences.text: Pending the contempt case, the respondent authorities have considered the case of the petitioners in W.P.No.33172 of 2011 and registered the plots in their favour.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is similarly placed as that of the petitioners in W.P.No.33172 of 2011.
The contempt case was disposed of by order dated 28.12.2012.
It is submitted that the petitioner is a senior citizen aged 64 years.
He paid total sale consideration for Plot No.91 of MIG category.
Due to circumstances beyond his control, he did not join the petitioners in W.P.No.33172 of 2011.

7. Learned Standing Counsel appearing for respondent No.3 submitted based on written instructions that the petitioner is not entitled for any relief as he has approached this Court after a gap of 30 years.
The petitioner and several others are defaulters, as such their allotments have been cancelled.
The petitioner cannot claim to be similarly placed as that of the petitioners in W.P.No.33172 of 2011 and Contempt Case No.2124 of 2012.
The value of the plots has been increased enormously since the date of initial allotment.
The Local Level Co-ordination Committee has resolved to go for fresh auction of all cancelled and left over plots.
Having known about the same, the petitioner approached this Court.
8. However, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is not a defaulter and the entire sale consideration has been paid by the petitioner.
Because of the disputes between respondent No.3 and the Wakf Board, 78 plots were not registered.

9. In the above circumstances, without entering into the merits, the writ petition is disposed of directing respondent No.3 to consider the representation of the petitioner dated 27.01.2025, for registration of Plot No.91 of MIG category situated at IDSMT Colony, Gadwal Town and Municipality, Jogulamba Gadwal District in his favour, within a period of four (04) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Until the representation of the petitioner is disposed of, the subject Plot No.91 of MIG category shall not be put to auction or allotted to third party.
No order as to costs.
As a sequel thereto, miscellaneous applications, if any, pending in the writ petition stand closed.
B. VIJAYSEN REDDY, J Date: 07.04.2025 vv B. Narender Goud, vs The State Of Telangana on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/12680300/
